In [[mathematics]], the '''identity theorem for [[Riemann surface]]s''' is a [[theorem]] that states that a [[holomorphic function]] is completely determined by its values  on any subset of its domain that has a [[limit point]].

==Statement of the theorem==
Let <math>X</math> and <math>Y</math> be Riemann surfaces, let <math>X</math> be connected, and let <math>f, g : X \to Y</math> be holomorphic. Suppose that <math>f|_{A} = g|_{A}</math> for some subset <math>A \subseteq X</math> that has a limit point, where <math>f|_{A} : A \to Y</math> denotes the [[restriction (mathematics)|restriction]] of <math>f</math> to <math>A</math>. Then <math>f = g</math> (on the whole of <math>X</math>).
